510: #### C11 Decide trust (internal, after every grade) [FR-MCP-AGENTCONTEXT-004]
511: 
512: - Trigger: C9 and C10 after their grade is saved. No endpoint.
513: - Rule: a response is `Trusted` only when it is not `Rejected`, `Stale`, or `Superseded`, its latest deterministic grade is `Pass`, and its latest model grade is `Pass` ("latest" as defined in section 6.3: greatest `GradedUtc`, then greatest `GradeId`); otherwise it is `Grading`. The decision runs in the same transaction as the grade insert, so concurrent grades each see a consistent latest pair.
514:

517:     S(["Grade saved"]) --> ST{"Response Rejected, Stale, or Superseded?"}

520:     D -->|no| G["Status Grading"]
521:     D -->|yes| M{"Latest model grade exists and Pass?"}
522:     M -->|no| G
523:     M -->|yes| T["Status Trusted, TrustedUtc set"]

742: #### C20 Run a stateless invocation (plugin) [FR-MCP-AGENTCONTEXT-009]

744: - Trigger: a delivered user request (Phase A Units A3 and A4) on a host whose plugin reads `Mode` through C1.

746: - Output: in `Stateless` mode the model receives only the rendered package and the request, without prior conversation turns; in `Pilot` mode the package is built and recorded but not injected; in `Off` nothing happens.
747: - A host recorded `turn_logging_unsupported` (Phase A, D6) has no minted turn, so C20 does not run there: the plugin stays stateful and reports `turn_logging_unsupported`, and the feature-matrix row records the limitation.

---
name: Requirements Management
description: Use when the user asks to "list requirements", "add requirement", "create FR", "create TR", "create test requirement", "generate requirements document", or "ingest requirements".
version: 0.1.0
---

# Requirements Management

## Overview

To manage functional requirements (FR), technical requirements (TR), test requirements (TEST), and their traceability mappings, use this plugin's declared hook/wrapper (or the REPL transport) for the `workflow.requirements.*` namespace. Do not substitute raw REST calls, generic `PowerShell.MCP wrapper`, helper modules, or another agent's plugin for normal requirements work.

The plugin wrapper validates documented params and emits single-line JSON to REPL stdio. Any direct REPL diagnostic call must use one single-line JSON request envelope, not formatted YAML.

The database is the source of truth for requirements. Markdown files are import/export projections only. Every operation is scoped to the workspace resolved from the signed marker, and generated workspace output must contain only the requested workspace's FR, TR, TEST, and traceability links.

## Initialization

Call `workflow.sessionlog.bootstrap` through this plugin's declared hook/wrapper to initialize the session log subsystem before issuing any workflow commands. This call is idempotent and should be made once per conversation context.

```yaml
type: request
payload:
  requestId: req-20260409T120000Z-bootstrap-001
  method: workflow.sessionlog.bootstrap
  params: {}
```

## Requirement Scope Layers

Plugin version 1.13.0 and newer exposes native layer operations. Treat this section as the layer API reference when plugin status reports these methods; do not ask the operator or inspect wrapper source just to learn the parameter shapes.

- `workflow.requirements.listLayers` / `req_list_layers` / `client.Requirements.ListRequirementLayersAsync`: omit params.
- `workflow.requirements.createLayer` / `req_create_layer` / `client.Requirements.CreateRequirementLayerAsync`: required params are `key`, `order`, and `name`; optional params are `description` and `scopeEndLayerKey`.
- `workflow.requirements.updateLayer` / `req_update_layer` / `client.Requirements.UpdateRequirementLayerAsync`: required param is `key`; optional params are `name`, `description`, and `scopeEndLayerKey`. Layer `order` is immutable; create a new layer rather than attempting to update `order`.
- `workflow.requirements.effective` / `req_effective` / `client.Requirements.GetEffectiveRequirementsAsync`: optional param is `layerKey`; omit `layerKey` to use the active workspace layer.

Use camelCase exactly in YAML:

```yaml
type: request
payload:
  requestId: req-20260409T115900Z-listlayers-001
  method: workflow.requirements.listLayers
  params: {}
```

```yaml
type: request
payload:
  requestId: req-20260409T115901Z-createlayer-001
  method: workflow.requirements.createLayer
  params:
    key: future
    order: 20
    name: Future Layer
    description: Requirements that are documented but not currently enforceable
```

```yaml
type: request
payload:
  requestId: req-20260409T115902Z-updatelayer-001
  method: workflow.requirements.updateLayer
  params:
    key: future
    name: Future Layer
    scopeEndLayerKey: release
```

```yaml
type: request
payload:
  requestId: req-20260409T115903Z-effective-001
  method: workflow.requirements.effective
  params:
    layerKey: future
```

FR, TR, TEST, and batch create/update commands also accept requirement scope fields:

- `scopeStartLayerKey`: first layer where the requirement is effective.
- `scopeEndLayerKey`: last layer where the requirement is effective; omit for open-ended scope.

Omit both fields for requirements that are effective in the default/current layer.

## Requirement ID Conventions

Three ID spaces are in use:

- **FR** - Functional Requirements: `^FR-[A-Z]+-\d{3}$`, e.g. `FR-MCP-001`, `FR-AUTH-042`
- **TR** - Technical Requirements: `^TR-[A-Z]+-[A-Z]+-\d{3}$`, e.g. `TR-MCP-ARCH-001`, `TR-AUTH-SEC-002`
- **TEST** - Test Requirements: `^TEST-[A-Z]+-\d{3}$`, e.g. `TEST-MCP-001`, `TEST-AUTH-003`

All IDs must be uppercase. TR IDs require both an area and a subarea segment; FR and TEST IDs require only an area segment.

## Functional Requirements (FR)

### Listing FRs

To retrieve a filtered list of functional requirements:

```yaml
type: request
payload:
  requestId: req-20260409T120000Z-listfr-001
  method: workflow.requirements.listFr
  params:
    area: MCP
    status: in_progress
```

All params are optional; omit to return all FRs. The result contains an `items` array:

```yaml
type: result
payload:
  requestId: req-20260409T120000Z-listfr-001
  result:
    items:
      - id: FR-MCP-001
        title: Agent authentication
        description: System must authenticate AI agents via API key
        status: completed
        priority: critical
        area: MCP
        createdAt: 2026-03-01T10:00:00Z
        updatedAt: 2026-04-09T12:00:00Z
    totalCount: 1
```

Valid `status` values: `pending`, `in_progress`, `completed`, `deferred`.

### Getting a Single FR

To fetch one functional requirement by ID:

```yaml
type: request
payload:
  requestId: req-20260409T120001Z-getfr-001
  method: workflow.requirements.getFr
  params:
    id: FR-MCP-001
```

### Creating an FR

To record a new functional requirement:

```yaml
type: request
payload:
  requestId: req-20260409T120002Z-createfr-001
  method: workflow.requirements.createFr
  params:
    id: FR-MCP-003
    title: Context search
    description: System must support semantic search across workspace documents
    priority: high
    area: MCP
    notes: Use hybrid search combining BM25 and vector embeddings
```

Required fields: `id`, `title`, `description`, `priority`, `area`. The `notes` field is optional.

### Acceptance Criteria

FR, TR, and TEST create/update commands accept structured `acceptanceCriteria` entries with the same shape used by TODO execution criteria:

```yaml
method: workflow.requirements.createFr
params:
  id: FR-MCP-XXX-001
  title: Acceptance criteria example
  description: Requirement records preserve structured pass/fail criteria.
  priority: high
  area: MCP
  acceptanceCriteria:
    - id: ac-1
      text: Round-trip preserves criterion text
      isSatisfied: false
    - id: ac-2
      text: Evidence is retained when supplied
      isSatisfied: true
      evidence: tests/Services/RequirementAcceptanceCriteriaTests.cs
```

To copy criteria from an execution TODO onto a requirement, call `workflow.requirements.copyAcceptanceCriteriaFromTodo`:

```yaml
method: workflow.requirements.copyAcceptanceCriteriaFromTodo
params:
  kind: fr
  id: FR-MCP-XXX-001
  todoId: PLAN-MCP-001
```

This maps to `POST /mcpserver/requirements/{kind}/{id}/acceptance-criteria/copy-from-todo` with body `{ "todoId": "PLAN-MCP-001" }`.

name: Triage Reporting
description: "Use when your agent discovers an incidental bug while working on another task and should submit it to MCP Server triage without changing focus. Triggers: 'triage', '/triage', 'submit a triage report', 'report an incidental bug', 'file this bug to triage', 'triage status'."
version: 0.1.0
---

# Triage Reporting

Use MCP Server triage for an incidental bug discovered while doing other work. Do not use triage for the user's active requested fix, assigned TODO, or current implementation target; fix that directly or track it through the normal TODO and requirements workflow.

Submit the report, then continue the current task. Do not expect immediate resolution, research, or TODO creation. Intake only returns the accepted queue state; background triage later groups reports, researches them, and may create a `BUG-TRIAGE-###` backlog TODO.

MCP Server-related reports, including MCP Server plugin bugs, are grouped into the registered `McpServer` workspace when that workspace exists. If no `McpServer` workspace is registered, the report stays in the submitting workspace.

## Tools

- Use `triage_report` to submit an incidental bug report.
- Native MCP clients may use `triage_status`; plugin/REPL callers must use schema-valid `workflow.triage.getReport`, `workflow.triage.getGroup`, or `workflow.triage.queryGroups` for status inspection.

## Report Shape

Include enough evidence for later research without leaving the active task:

- `title`: short problem statement.
- `summary`: observed failure and why it matters.
- `component`: product area, package, or plugin name.
- `affectedPaths`: relevant paths when known.
- `affectedSymbols`: relevant methods, commands, or API names when known.
- `errorSignature`: stable error text, status code, or exception type when known.
- `dedupeKey`: stable key when the same bug may be reported again.
- `evidence`: compact command output or reproduction context.

## REPL Example

```yaml
type: request
payload:
  requestId: req-20260625T120000Z-triage-report
  method: workflow.triage.report
  params:
    title: Plugin wrapper hides triage_report validation errors
    summary: The wrapper exits with success after a triage_report validation failure, masking the error.
    component: mcpserver-plugin
    affectedPaths:
      - lib/repl-invoke.ps1
    errorSignature: triage_validation_hidden
    reporterAgent: <your-agent>
```

After a successful response, record the returned `reportId`, `groupId`, `status`, and `quietDeadlineUtc` only if useful for the current audit trail, then continue the current task.

## PowerShell Object-Safe Example

When using the plugin PowerShell surface, prefer the exported shim helpers and `-ParamsObject` so the wrapper serializes the YAML payload:

```powershell
Import-Module (Join-Path $env:MCP_PLUGIN_ROOT 'lib/McpPluginShim.psm1') -Force
$params = New-McpTriageReportParams `
    -Title 'Plugin wrapper hides triage validation errors' `
    -Summary 'workflow.triage.report failures are not visible to the agent.' `
    -Component 'mcpserver-plugin' `
    -AffectedPaths @('lib/repl-invoke.ps1') `
    -ErrorSignature 'triage_validation_hidden' `
    -ReporterAgent '<your-agent>'
& (Join-Path $env:MCP_PLUGIN_ROOT 'lib/Invoke-McpPlugin.ps1') -Command Invoke -Method workflow.triage.report -ParamsObject $params
```

Use `New-McpTriageGetReportParams`, `New-McpTriageGetGroupParams`, and `New-McpTriageQueryGroupsParams` for object-safe status inspection through `workflow.triage.getReport`, `workflow.triage.getGroup`, and `workflow.triage.queryGroups`.

2: # Architecture: Turn Logging, Turn Reviews, and Stateless Agent Context
3: 
4: Status: architecture documentation of the merged plan PLAN-SESSIONTURNREVIEW-001 (`docs/plans/PLAN-SESSIONTURN-SESSIONREVIEW-001.md`), pending operator approval of the merged plan. Operator directives (2026-10-11, verbatim): "Integrate attached to current plan.", "Reconstruct plan with added requirements", "Also publish the doc to develop", "Outline now, catalog in P0", "No new code until I approve merged plan.", "I want every model defined.  I want every unit of work request and respone defined.  I want every endpoint defined.", and "I want a single, complete activity diagram (mermaid) for every unit of work.  I want sequence diagrams for submitting each request type and processing every response.  I want a md doc describing the who plan as architecture documentation."
5: 
6: This document describes the whole merged plan as architecture: the components, the data each part owns, every unit of work with its request, response, and error contract, one complete activity diagram per unit of work, and sequence diagrams for submitting each request type and processing each response. The plan document remains the authority for slices, gates, tests, and acceptance criteria; the agent-context contracts are specified in `docs/Stateless-Agent-Context-Management.md`, and this document repeats them so it stands alone.
7: 
8: How to read the diagrams:
9: 
10: - Activity diagrams are Mermaid flowcharts read top to bottom. A rounded terminal is a start or an end, a diamond is a decision, a rectangle is an action, and every error exit is drawn and ends in a terminal that names the error code.
11: - Sequence diagrams show who sends what. Each `alt` block lists every response the caller can receive and how the caller processes it.
12: - Requirement ids in brackets name the functional requirement the unit of work realizes. Ids of the form `FR-MCP-AGENTCONTEXT-*` are reserved for P0, where the agent-context catalog is created.
13: 
14: ## 1. Goals
15: 
16: 1. One user request is exactly one session-log turn, minted by the server when the message arrives, and every write lands on the turn of the request that caused it (Phase A).
17: 2. Every turn carries a request class and two review records (agent and hostile) with lossless decimal scores, a status lifecycle, configurable thresholds, and a server-enforced completion gate (Phase B).
18: 3. Every agent invocation can run stateless: the server builds a bounded, reproducible context package from the profile, rules, requirements, session-log evidence, trusted prior responses, and current code, and only responses graded at 98/98 with no FAIL or UNKNOWN become trusted context for later requests (Phase C).
19: 
20: Phase C depends on Phase A (turns are the unit a package is built for, and session-log turns are evidence) and on Phase B (the review thresholds and the 98/98 grading rule).
21:

72: ## 3. Cross-cutting conventions
73: 
74: - Workspace scoping: every request is scoped to one workspace through the `X-Workspace-Path` header (REST), the `workspacePath` parameter (MCP tools, REPL), or `MCP_WORKSPACE_PATH` (plugins). Every stored record carries its `WorkspaceId`, and no read ever crosses workspaces.
75: - Authentication: `X-Api-Key` (or `api_key`) from the workspace marker. Plugins never call REST directly; they use the REPL wrapper.
76: - Routes: every REST route exists under `/qbrainai/...` with the legacy alias `/mcpserver/...`.
77: - Errors: a REST error body is `{ "error": "<code>", "message": "<text>", "details": { ... } }`; validation failures are 400, conflicts 409 or 422 as stated per unit, missing resources 404. The REPL error envelope is `type: error` with `code`, `message`, and `retryable`.
78: - Identifiers: session ids `<Agent>-<yyyyMMddTHHmmssZ>-<suffix>`; server-minted request ids `req-<yyyyMMddTHHmmssZ>-<8 hex>`; agent-context record ids are prefixed GUIDs (section 7.2).
79: - Root ids: every record carries the root ids of its parents (workspace, MCP session, request, and for agent context the package and response).
80: - Secrets: no API key, token, password, or credential is ever stored in a turn field, a context package, or a response; the session-log sanitizer and the agent-context secret filter redact on write and on every read surface.
81: - Process: every slice follows the Byrd Development Process v4 (requirements, tests red, mocks green, implementation green, full gates with zero failures and zero skips) and ends with a Codex gpt-6-sol xhigh hostile validation at accuracy and completeness of at least 98 with every claim PASS. Builds and tests run as Nuke targets natively on Windows or Linux; GitHub Actions and Azure Pipelines are not part of any requirement or process; Octopus (container on LAB-OMARCHY) is used only for releases.
82: 
83: ## 4. Phase A: correct, independent turn logging
84: 
85: ### 4.1 Components and data
86: 
87: - Server: `SessionLogService.SubmitWithOutcomesAsync` (per-turn outcomes), `ISessionLogService.MintTurnAsync`, `ISessionLogRequestIdMinter`, `ISessionLogTurnUpsertGuard`, `SessionLogTurnEntity.IngressNonce` (unique filtered index per MCP session).
88: - PowerShell plugin core (`plugins/core/lib-ps`): prompt hook, arrival bridge (claude-code, claude-cowork), `Sync-PluginArrivalLog`, verb binding (`New-ReplInvocationBinding`, `Resolve-ReplTargetTurn`), truthful persist (`Get-ReplTurnWriteOutcome`, `Invoke-ReplPersistTurn`), failsafe and alias journal, Stop gate (`Get-PluginStopGateTurns`, pure `Get-PluginStopGateFindings`).
89: - Node plugin core (`plugins/core/lib-node`): the same contracts in TypeScript for cline, cline-v2, and opencode (`classifySystemEvent`, `ingressNonce`, `mintRequest`, `bindInvocation`, `resolveTargetTurn`, `mapTurnWriteOutcome`, alias consumers).
90: - Plugin per-host-session state (one directory per host session key under the plugin cache):
91:   - `turns/<requestId>.yaml` with its own lock `turns/<requestId>.lock`: one file per turn.
92:   - `sessions/<hostSessionKey>/turn-state.yaml`: `writeTarget { requestId, deliveredAtUtc, source }`, `openDelivered [requestId]`, `queue [{ kind, requestId, nonce, enqueueOffset, enqueueTimestamp, promptSha256, state, stateOffset, mintedAtUtc }]`, `appliedThroughOffset`, `mcpSessionId`, `ledger [...]`, `unsupportedSince { causeOffset, causeOperation, reason }`; every entry carries the root ids; written by one atomic replace under `turn-open.lock`.
93:   - `sessions/<hostSessionKey>/ended.yaml` (`reason: session_end`), `sessions/<hostSessionKey>/aliases.yaml` (alias journal), `sessions/<key>/arrival-bridge.pid`.
94:   - `current-turn.yaml` is a read-only legacy status file and is never used for targeting.
95: 
96: Request lifecycle (plugin queue entry):
97: 
98: ```mermaid
99: stateDiagram-v2
100:     [*] --> queued: enqueue (mint)
101:     queued --> delivered: dequeue of head, or remove with absorbed_mid_turn
102:     queued --> withdrawn: remove with another or no reason, or popAll
103:     delivered --> closed: completeTurn or failTurn confirmed by server
104:     withdrawn --> closed: failTurn "withdrawn before delivery" confirmed
105:     closed --> [*]
106: ```

108: ### 4.2 Unit A1: Mint a turn at ingress [FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-001]
109: 
110: - Trigger: a user message arrives at a host arrival mechanism (prompt hook, arrival bridge, or host-native adapter). Only hooks and adapters call it; there is no MCP tool, and the plugin wrapper refuses a model-originated call with `mint_requires_host_ingress`.
111: - Surfaces: `POST /qbrainai/sessionlog/{agent}/{sessionId}/mint` (alias `/mcpserver/...`), client `MintTurnAsync`, REPL `workflow.sessionlog.mintTurn`.
112: - Request `SessionLogMintTurnRequest`: `ingressNonce` (string, required: the host's per-message id or a SHA-256 of host event fields), `queryTitle`, `queryText`, `model`, `planFile` (value or the `None` sentinel), `todoId` (value or `None`).
113: - Response `SessionLogMintTurnResult`: `requestId` (`req-<yyyyMMddTHHmmssZ>-<8 hex>`), `outcome` (`created` or `merged`), `storedStatus`.
114:   - 201 `created`: a new in-progress turn.
115:   - 200 `merged`: the same nonce was already minted in this MCP session; the same `requestId` is returned and a terminal turn is not reopened.
116: - Errors: 400 `validation_error` (missing nonce, invalid `planFile` or `todoId`), 404 with detail code `session_not_open`, 500 with final detail code `mint_collision_exhausted` after six request-id collisions.
117: 
118: ```mermaid
119: flowchart TD
120:     S(["Mint request received"]) --> V{"Body valid: nonce present, planFile and todoId valid?"}
121:     V -->|no| E400(["400 validation_error"])
122:     V -->|yes| O{"MCP session open for agent and sessionId?"}
123:     O -->|no| E404(["404 session_not_open"])
124:     O -->|yes| N{"Turn with this ingressNonce exists in the session?"}
125:     N -->|yes| M(["200 merged: existing requestId and storedStatus, status unchanged"])
126:     N -->|no| K["attempt = 1"]
127:     K --> G["Minter generates req-UTC-8hex"]
128:     G --> I["Insert in-progress turn with ingressNonce"]
129:     I --> R{"Insert result"}
130:     R -->|success| C(["201 created: requestId, storedStatus in_progress"])
131:     R -->|nonce unique index violated by a concurrent mint| X["Read the turn that holds the nonce"]
132:     X --> M
133:     R -->|requestId unique index violated| A{"attempt less than 6?"}
134:     A -->|yes| B["attempt = attempt + 1"]
135:     B --> G
136:     A -->|no| E500(["500 mint_collision_exhausted"])
137: ```

139: ### 4.3 Unit A2: Submit a session log with per-turn outcomes [FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-004]
140: 
141: - Surfaces: `POST /qbrainai/sessionlog` (existing route), MCP `sessionlog_submit`, client `SubmitAsync`, REPL submit.
142: - Request: the unified session-log document (`UnifiedSessionLogDto`) with its turns.
143: - Response 201 `SessionLogSubmitResult`: existing fields plus `turns: [{ requestId, outcome, storedStatus, reason }]`, where `outcome` is `created`, `merged`, or `skipped_terminal`. MCP returns `{ success, id, turns }`. The status code stays 201.
144: - Rules: an identical resubmit is `merged` with reason `no_change`; duplicate request ids in one submission apply last-wins with one outcome each; a write that would move a terminal turn is `skipped_terminal` and changes nothing; there is no `skipped_duplicate` outcome.
145: 
146: ```mermaid
147: flowchart TD
148:     S(["Submit received"]) --> P{"Document parses?"}
149:     P -->|no| E400(["400 validation_error"])
150:     P -->|yes| D["Collapse duplicate requestIds last-wins"]
151:     D --> L["For each turn in the submission"]
152:     L --> F{"Turn exists in store?"}
153:     F -->|no| CR["Insert turn: outcome created"]
154:     F -->|yes| T{"Stored turn terminal and incoming write would change it?"}
155:     T -->|yes| SK["Leave stored turn unchanged: outcome skipped_terminal with storedStatus and reason"]
156:     T -->|no| Q{"Incoming equals stored?"}
157:     Q -->|yes| NC["outcome merged, reason no_change"]
158:     Q -->|no| MG["Merge fields: outcome merged"]
159:     CR --> NX{"More turns?"}
160:     SK --> NX
161:     NC --> NX
162:     MG --> NX
163:     NX -->|yes| L
164:     NX -->|no| SV["Save changes in one transaction"]
165:     SV --> R(["201 with turns outcome list"])
166: ```

218: ### 4.5 Unit A4: Open a turn from the prompt hook (hosts without a bridge) [FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-001, FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-002, FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-003]
219: 
220: - Hosts: codex, grok, grok-bot, copilot (PowerShell core), and classic cline (Node core) through its native-hook adapter; cline-v2 and opencode through their handlers.
221: - Input: the host's prompt hook payload. Output: a delivered request and write target, or a hook status.
222: - Hook statuses: `turn-opened`, `turn-already-open`, `system-event-skipped`, `turn-open-contended`, `turn-open-failed` (reason `nonce_source_missing` or the server code), `turn_logging_unsupported`.
223: 
224: ```mermaid
225: flowchart TD
226:     S(["Prompt hook fires"]) --> UNS{"Host supported for turn logging and its P0.2 row passed?"}
227:     UNS -->|no| UL(["turn_logging_unsupported: no mint, no write"])
228:     UNS -->|yes| SYS{"System event: task-notification, agent-message, agent_id, subagentType, or subagent env marker?"}
229:     SYS -->|yes| SK(["system-event-skipped: no mint"])
230:     SYS -->|no| LK{"turn-open.lock acquired?"}
231:     LK -->|no| CT(["turn-open-contended: no mint"])
232:     LK -->|yes| NN{"Host nonce field present?"}
233:     NN -->|no| NF(["turn-open-failed nonce_source_missing: failsafe diagnostic, no invented nonce"])
234:     NN -->|yes| MN["Mint with the host nonce (Unit A1)"]
235:     MN --> MR{"Mint result"}
236:     MR -->|created| DV["Deliver: write target, openDelivered, ledger entry"]
237:     DV --> OK(["turn-opened"])
238:     MR -->|merged, turn in progress| EQ{"Equal-field host (copilot or classic cline) and a new invocation?"}
239:     EQ -->|yes| FC(["Fail closed: unsupportedSince indistinguishable_arrival"])
240:     EQ -->|no| AO(["turn-already-open: rebind to the same requestId"])
241:     MR -->|merged, turn terminal| TT(["Report storedStatus: not write target, not open, not ledgered"])
242:     MR -->|outage| PD["Open pending-nonce locally, failsafe mint record"]
243:     PD --> PO(["turn-opened pending: drained later (Unit A7)"])
244:     MR -->|final refusal| FR(["turn-open-failed with the server code"])
245: ```

247: ### 4.6 Unit A5: Bind a session-log verb to its turn [FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-007]
248: 
249: - Verbs: `appendActions`, `appendDialog`, `appendDecisions`, `updateTurn`, `completeTurn`, `failTurn`, `setTurnTitle`, and from Phase B `recordReview`.
250: - Request: the verb's payload plus an optional explicit `requestId`, or a trusted recovery pair (`sessionId`, `requestId`).
251: - Response: the resolved target request id and an immutable invocation binding `{ hostSessionKey, keySource, ingressNonce, requestId, boundAtUtc }` stored with the persist and failsafe records; or a refusal code.
252: - Refusal codes: `request_unknown`, `request_ambiguous`, `turn_immutable`, `host_session_unknown`, `host_session_ambiguous`, `turn_logging_unsupported`; warning `host_session_inferred`.
253: 
254: ```mermaid
255: flowchart TD
256:     S(["Verb invoked"]) --> SY["Sync-PluginArrivalLog up to the transcript length at start"]
257:     SY --> KEY{"Host session key readable from the invocation context?"}
258:     KEY -->|no| PAIR{"Trusted pair sessionId and requestId supplied and verified on the server?"}
259:     PAIR -->|yes| BP["Bind to the pair"]
260:     PAIR -->|no| LIVE{"Live host sessions of this agent in the workspace"}
261:     LIVE -->|none| HU(["Refuse host_session_unknown"])
262:     LIVE -->|more than one| HA(["Refuse host_session_ambiguous"])
263:     LIVE -->|exactly one| INF["Use it: warning host_session_inferred"]
264:     KEY -->|yes| KS["Load sessions/key/turn-state.yaml"]
265:     INF --> KS
266:     KS --> UNS{"unsupportedSince recorded?"}
267:     UNS -->|yes| OPN{"Target is a turn already open when the session failed closed?"}
268:     OPN -->|yes| FS(["Bind and capture the write to the failsafe as unsupported_session"])
269:     OPN -->|no| UL(["Refuse turn_logging_unsupported"])
270:     UNS -->|no| EXP{"Explicit requestId supplied?"}
271:     EXP -->|yes| KN{"Known open turn of this MCP session?"}
272:     KN -->|no| RU(["Refuse request_unknown"])
273:     KN -->|yes| TERM
274:     EXP -->|no| CNT{"Delivered requests open"}
275:     CNT -->|two or more| AMB(["Refuse request_ambiguous naming the open requests"])
276:     CNT -->|none| NT{"Write target set?"}
277:     NT -->|no| RU2(["Refuse request_unknown naming the host session key"])
278:     NT -->|yes, closed| IM(["Refuse turn_immutable naming the write target"])
279:     CNT -->|exactly one| WT["Target = write target"]
280:     WT --> TERM{"Target locally terminal?"}
281:     BP --> TERM
282:     TERM -->|yes, verb not recordReview or class-only| IM2(["Refuse turn_immutable"])
283:     TERM -->|no, or review or class-only update| B(["Binding captured once: proceed to persist (Unit A6)"])
284: ```

286: ### 4.7 Unit A6: Persist a turn write with a truthful receipt [FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-004]
287: 
288: - Request: a turn upsert (`POST /qbrainai/sessionlog/{agent}/{sessionId}/turn`, `PATCH` or `PUT .../{requestId}`, `POST .../complete` or `.../fail`) built by `New-McpPluginTurnUpsertRequest` with the binding.
289: - Response (plugin receipt): `persisted` (bool), `code` (`persisted`, `skipped_terminal`, `queued`, or the server error code), `storedStatus`, `reason`; exit code 0 or 1.
290: 
291: ```mermaid
292: flowchart TD
293:     S(["Bound write ready"]) --> SEND["Send upsert through the REPL"]
294:     SEND --> RES{"Result"}
295:     RES -->|transport outage| FQ["Write failsafe record keyed by the bound requestId"]
296:     FQ --> QD(["Receipt persisted false, code queued: degraded persistence, exit 1"])
297:     RES -->|server error| ER{"Error code"}
298:     ER -->|session_turn_completion_gate| GR["Record the server refusal and missing items locally: turn stays in progress"]
299:     GR --> GRE(["Receipt persisted false with the server message and missing items, exit 1"])
300:     ER -->|other| OE(["Receipt persisted false with the server code, exit 1"])
301:     RES -->|turns outcome list| OUT{"Outcome for the bound requestId"}
302:     OUT -->|created or merged| CL{"Close verb?"}
303:     CL -->|yes| RM["Remove from openDelivered and the ledger after the confirmed close"]
304:     CL -->|no| OK
305:     RM --> OK(["Receipt persisted true, code persisted, storedStatus: failsafe cleared, exit 0"])
306:     OUT -->|skipped_terminal| TS["Cache storedStatus as terminal: later verbs refused locally with turn_immutable"]
307:     TS --> SKR(["Receipt persisted false, code skipped_terminal, failsafe cleared, exit 1"])
308: ```

310: ### 4.8 Unit A7: Drain the failsafe [FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-001, FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-004, FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-005]
311: 
312: - Trigger: SessionStart, and the next verb after an outage.
313: - Input: failsafe records in their original order, each with its captured binding and root-id envelope.
314: - Output: minted ids journaled as aliases, writes replayed onto their own turns, records removed only after a confirmed result.
315: 
316: ```mermaid
317: flowchart TD
318:     S(["Drain starts"]) --> NX{"Next record"}
319:     NX -->|none| E(["Drain complete"])
320:     NX -->|record| LB{"Record has a captured binding?"}
321:     LB -->|no, legacy| KEEP["Retain, never auto-replay, warn at Stop"]
322:     KEEP --> NX
323:     LB -->|yes| SO["Replay idempotent session open for the envelope mcpSessionId"]
324:     SO --> SOR{"Session open confirmed?"}
325:     SOR -->|outage| STOP(["Stop drain: records retained"])
326:     SOR -->|yes| KIND{"Record kind"}
327:     KIND -->|mint| MT["Mint with the original nonce (Unit A1)"]
328:     MT --> MTR{"Mint result"}
329:     MTR -->|session_not_open after confirmed open| FIN["Final: turn-open-failed, record removed"]
330:     FIN --> NX
331:     MTR -->|outage| STOP
332:     MTR -->|created or merged| AJ["Journal alias pending-nonce to requestId in aliases.yaml"]
333:     AJ --> RW["Rewrite queued records of that alias to the minted id"]
334:     RW --> RMV["Remove the mint record"]
335:     RMV --> NX
336:     KIND -->|write| AL{"Write under a pending id with a journaled alias?"}
337:     AL -->|yes| SUB["Send under the minted id"]
338:     AL -->|no| SEND["Send under its bound id"]

343:     DONE --> NX

348: ### 4.9 Unit A8: Evaluate the Stop gate [FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-005]
349: 
350: - Trigger: every host Stop (Claude Code `stop_hook_active`, Grok `stopHookActive`; the Node stop-equivalent on Node hosts).
351: - Output: `{}` (pass) or a block whose text is `session_turn_stop_gate: <n> turn(s) are not closed correctly:` followed by one line per turn `<id> (<code>): <remedy>` and `The stop gate never closes turns for you.`; warnings in either case. The gate never completes or fails a turn.
352: 
353: ```mermaid
354: flowchart TD
355:     S(["Stop event"]) --> AP["Apply pending transcript records up to the transcript length at Stop start"]
356:     AP --> LD["Load this host session's ledger, open list, withdrawn entries, and failsafe"]
357:     LD --> FD["Compute findings with the pure function (no IO)"]
358:     FD --> EACH{"For each turn of this host session"}
359:     EACH --> REF{"Most recent close refused by the server with session_turn_completion_gate?"}
360:     REF -->|yes| B1["Block session_turn_completion_gate: server missing items first"]
361:     REF -->|no| WDR{"Withdrawn and still in progress?"}
362:     WDR -->|yes| B2["Block turn_withdrawn_unclosed: remedy failTurn withdrawn before delivery"]
363:     WDR -->|no| DLV{"Delivered and still in progress?"}
364:     DLV -->|yes| UNS{"Session unsupportedSince and the close is captured in the failsafe?"}
365:     UNS -->|yes| W1["Warn: unsupported session, drained at next SessionStart"]
366:     UNS -->|no| OUTG{"Model close held in the failsafe by an outage?"}

800: ### 5.4 Unit B3: Reset a review section [FR-SUPPORT-016, FR-MCP-SESSIONREVIEW-001]
801: 
802: - Surface: `DELETE /qbrainai/sessionlog/{agent}/{sessionId}/{requestId}/sections/{section}`; client `ClearTurnReviewAsync`. Item delete `DELETE .../sections/{section}/items/{itemKey}` on a review section is rejected.
803: - Response: the record reset to the creation default for the turn's current class.
804: - Errors: 400 `review_section_reset_on_terminal_turn` (record unchanged), 400 on item delete.

809:     IT -->|yes| E1(["400: items cannot be deleted from a review section"])
810:     IT -->|no| TS{"Turn completed or failed?"}

812:     TS -->|no| DEF{"Hostile kind and class Chore?"}

819: ### 5.5 Unit B4: Complete or fail under the completion gate [FR-MCP-SESSIONCLASS-002, -003, -004]
820: 
821: - Surfaces: every transition path to `completed` or `failed` (upsert, PATCH, PUT, lifecycle complete and fail, submit).
822: - Policy: `completed` needs `requestClass` and `agentReview.status` in Pass, Fail, or Other; for Code and Docs also `hostileReview.status` in Pass, Fail, or Other; for Chore the hostile review is not checked. `failed` needs `requestClass` only. `canceled` is not gated. Only the transition is gated; terminal enrichment is not re-gated.
823: - Exempt origins: ServerInternal (`AuditedAgentCliClient`, `WorkspacePolicyService`, `QuadBrainOpenAiChatService`), Replication (federation apply), Import (`SessionLogIngestor`, `TranscriptSessionLogPersister`). Gated: Agent (all external surfaces), `QuadBrainInternalToolExecutor`, REPL importRecovery.
824: - Error: 400 `session_turn_completion_gate`, message token-prefixed and listing the missing items in the order requestClass, agentReview, hostileReview; the whole write is rejected atomically.

855: - Plugin side (`ConvertFrom-McpHvReceipt`, Node mapper): input the reviewer's JSON receipt and the response jsonl; output a `recordReview` payload with `correctness = accuracy/100`, `completeness = completeness/100` as exact decimals, `reasons`, `reviewer`, `reviewedAt`, both jsonl paths, and `hvVerdict`.

35:- Queued-message arrival (operator D5, 2026-10-09: "Arrival bridge"): a message the operator sends while a turn is running is minted when it is enqueued, not when the model later processes it. On hosts that record the enqueue in a transcript (Claude Code), a per-host-session arrival bridge started by the SessionStart hook tails the transcript and follows each queued message through the lifecycle the transcript records. Observed in this workspace's Claude Code transcripts on 2026-10-09: 117 `enqueue`, 79 `dequeue`, 35 `remove` (27 with reason `absorbed_mid_turn`), 2 `popAll`; a normal prompt is `enqueue` then `dequeue` within milliseconds, a mid-turn message is `enqueue` then `remove` with `absorbed_mid_turn` when it is injected into the running turn (for example the operator's mid-turn message beginning "write a global memory with the" was removed with `absorbed_mid_turn` at 2026-10-09T14:35:47.730Z), and `popAll` pulls queued text back into the input box. The bridge mints at `enqueue` (state `queued`); the request becomes `delivered` at `dequeue` (applied by the bridge from the transcript itself; on hosts with a bridge the prompt hook neither mints nor claims) or at `remove` with `absorbed_mid_turn`; it becomes `withdrawn` at `popAll` or a `remove` with any other or no reason. Task notifications and other system events that the host also enqueues are classified and never minted; on bridge hosts they keep their queue position (`kind: system`), so their `dequeue` never delivers a user request.
110:- claude-code: nonce: the bridge's `q-` enqueue nonce (the bridge is the only minter, FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-001-AC009); hook key payload `session_id`; verb key env `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID` read at verb start in shell, PowerShell, and hook subprocesses (equals `session_id`; those subprocesses see the updated value after `/clear`); stdio MCP verbs use the live-session rule; payloads carrying `agent_id` are subagent events (system events, no turn); the subagent's own Bash and PowerShell verbs carry the parent's `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID` and bind to the parent's write target; stop uses payload `stop_hook_active`. Arrival bridge (D5), the only minter on claude-code (known-good single source of truth: the host transcript is one ordered log written by one producer, so the bridge needs no key shared with the hook, which the host does not provide: Claude Code's `queue-operation` records carry no `promptId` although its user records do): started by SessionStart with the payload `transcript_path`, it applies `queue-operation` lines in file order. Every `enqueue` takes a queue position, so FIFO `dequeue` stays exact. An `enqueue` whose `content` the system-event classifier marks as a system event is added as `{ kind: system, enqueueOffset, enqueueTimestamp, promptSha256, state: queued }` with the session-level envelope `{ workspacePath, agent, mcpSessionId, hostSessionKey }` (it has no nonce or requestId, and none is ever invented for it) and is never minted. An `enqueue` whose `content` the classifier accepts as a user request: mint with nonce `q-` + SHA-256(`session_id` LF the record's starting byte offset in the transcript LF enqueue `timestamp` LF `content`) truncated to 62 hex characters (the offset is unique per record and identical on replay, so two distinct records with equal timestamp and content get two nonces), and add `{ kind: request, requestId, nonce, enqueueOffset, enqueueTimestamp, promptSha256, state: queued, stateOffset, mintedAtUtc }` with the root-id envelope to the queue in `sessions/<key>/turn-state.yaml`. `dequeue` (no content) removes the head of the host session's `queued` entries: a `kind: request` head becomes `delivered` and the write target; a `kind: system` head is removed and delivers nothing. `remove` and `popAll` records that match a `kind: system` entry drop it without a turn. `remove` with reason `absorbed_mid_turn`: the `queued` entry whose `promptSha256` equals the record's `content` hash (both written by the same producer) becomes `delivered` and the write target when exactly one queued entry has that hash. `remove` with any other or no reason: the matching `queued` entry becomes `withdrawn` when exactly one queued entry has that content hash. `popAll`: when, for every content line it carries, the number of lines with that content equals the number of queued entries with that content hash, those entries become `withdrawn`. Fail-closed rule (D6): a `remove` carries `commandUuid` and `deliveryId` (Claude Code 2.1.293), which also appear on the delivered message's `queued_command` attachment, but `enqueue` and `dequeue` carry no key shared with it, so a `remove` that matches two or more queued entries, or a `popAll` that carries fewer lines of a content than there are queued entries with that content, cannot be attributed (a `popAll` whose line count equals the matching entry count withdraws them all, because every candidate is withdrawn). The bridge never guesses: at the first such record it stops before it without advancing `appliedThroughOffset`, sets `turn-state.yaml` `unsupportedSince: { causeOffset, causeOperation, reason: queue_removal_ambiguous }`, and from then on every session-log verb in that host session reports `turn_logging_unsupported` and writes nothing to the server until the session ends, except that writes for a turn already open at that moment go to the plugin failsafe (FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-005-AC001). Turns that are open at that moment are left exactly as they are on the server, the stop gate blocks on each only until the model's close of it is captured in the plugin failsafe and then warns `queue_removal_ambiguous` listing them (FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-005-AC001), and the next SessionStart for the agent lists them with their original (MCP `sessionId`, `requestId`) pairs for closing through the trusted recovery flow (FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-005-AC006). P0.2 records the `remove` identity fields; the bridge never uses them to pair with an `enqueue`. Only `queue-operation` lines are arrival records; every other record type is ignored by design. A `queue-operation` with an unknown operation or a missing required field is never skipped: the bridge stops before it without advancing `appliedThroughOffset`, records warning `arrival_bridge_format_unrecognized` and, after a delivered request, `unsupportedSince` with that reason and the record's `causeOffset` in the same atomic replace (unsupported-session rule), and the host session reports `turn_logging_unsupported` on every session-log verb (D6) until a verified adapter handles that shape, while writes for a turn already open go to the plugin failsafe (FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-005-AC001). Each record's state change and the advance of `appliedThroughOffset` past it are one atomic replace of `turn-state.yaml` (temp file, flush, rename, under `turn-open.lock`); records that start below `appliedThroughOffset` are skipped, so a restart never re-applies a record; the server mint for `enqueue` happens before that replace and is idempotent (same nonce, `merged`). Records are applied by whichever process holds `turn-open.lock`: the bridge, or a session-log verb, which first records the transcript length at the moment the invocation starts and, after taking the lock, applies every pending record that ends at or before that length, never a record appended later, before it binds (FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-007-AC006), so a verb started after a `dequeue` line was written binds to that request, and a `dequeue` appended after the verb started never retargets it (D2). The prompt hook on claude-code and claude-cowork neither mints nor claims; it classifies system events and starts no turn. P0.2 verifies that every user prompt (in each prompt form of FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-001-AC009) produces an `enqueue` record and that `dequeue` always takes the head; if either fails, claude-code is `turn_logging_unsupported` (D6) until an adapter with a traceable key exists, recorded in the feature matrix.
231:- FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-001-AC010 Queue lifecycle: a `queued` request becomes `delivered` (and the host session's write target) at `dequeue` (the head of the queue) or at `remove` with reason `absorbed_mid_turn`, and becomes `withdrawn` at a `popAll` or a `remove` with any other or no reason; minting never moves the write target; a withdrawn request stays `in_progress` on the server until the model closes it (FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-005-AC009). A record that cannot be attributed to exactly one queued entry (equal content with no shared key: a `remove` matching two or more entries, or a `popAll` carrying fewer lines of a content than there are matching entries) is never guessed: the host session fails closed under D6 (the bridge stops before the record, `unsupportedSince` is recorded, every session-log verb in that host session reports `turn_logging_unsupported` and writes nothing to the server until it ends, writes for its already open turns go to the plugin failsafe and drain at the next SessionStart (FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-005-AC001), and its open turns are listed with their pairs at the next SessionStart); a `popAll` whose line count equals the matching entry count withdraws them all. Every `enqueue` takes a queue position: system events as unminted `kind: system` entries, so a `dequeue` whose head is a system entry delivers nothing and the user request behind it stays `queued` until its own delivery (FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-002-AC001). [A3 +A4]

The instruction text includes a designDecision and, from S8/S9 (when the plugin's requestClass and recordReview verbs ship), the `requestClass` the close needs, so following it exactly makes the next Stop pass (`StopGate_WithdrawnFailedPerInstruction_NextStopPasses`). docs/architecture/SessionTurn-Review-AgentContext-Architecture.md:72 ## 3. Cross-cutting conventions
docs/architecture/SessionTurn-Review-AgentContext-Architecture.md:73 
docs/architecture/SessionTurn-Review-AgentContext-Architecture.md:74 - Workspace scoping: every request is scoped to one workspace through the `X-Workspace-Path` header (REST), the `workspacePath` parameter (MCP tools, REPL), or `MCP_WORKSPACE_PATH` (plugins). Every stored record carries its `WorkspaceId`, and no read ever crosses workspaces.
docs/architecture/SessionTurn-Review-AgentContext-Architecture.md:75 - Authentication: `X-Api-Key` (or `api_key`) from the workspace marker. Plugins never call REST directly; they use the REPL wrapper.
docs/architecture/SessionTurn-Review-AgentContext-Architecture.md:76 - Routes: every REST route exists under `/qbrainai/...` with the legacy alias `/mcpserver/...`.
docs/architecture/SessionTurn-Review-AgentContext-Architecture.md:77 - Errors: a REST error body is `{ "error": "<code>", "message": "<text>", "details": { ... } }`; validation failures are 400, conflicts 409 or 422 as stated per unit, missing resources 404. The REPL error envelope is `type: error` with `code`, `message`, and `retryable`.
docs/architecture/SessionTurn-Review-AgentContext-Architecture.md:78 - Identifiers: session ids `<Agent>-<yyyyMMddTHHmmssZ>-<suffix>`; server-minted request ids `req-<yyyyMMddTHHmmssZ>-<8 hex>`; agent-context record ids are prefixed GUIDs (section 7.2).
docs/architecture/SessionTurn-Review-AgentContext-Architecture.md:79 - Root ids: every record carries the root ids of its parents (workspace, MCP session, request, and for agent context the package and response).
docs/architecture/SessionTurn-Review-AgentContext-Architecture.md:80 - Secrets: no API key, token, password, or credential is ever stored in a turn field, a context package, or a response; the session-log sanitizer and the agent-context secret filter redact on write and on every read surface.
docs/architecture/SessionTurn-Review-AgentContext-Architecture.md:81 - Process: every slice follows the Byrd Development Process v4 (requirements, tests red, mocks green, implementation green, full gates with zero failures and zero skips) and ends with a Codex gpt-6-sol xhigh hostile validation at accuracy and completeness of at least 98 with every claim PASS. Builds and tests run as Nuke targets natively on Windows or Linux; GitHub Actions and Azure Pipelines are not part of any requirement or process; Octopus (container on LAB-OMARCHY) is used only for releases.
